subject: cm1
title: Discount Rate from Interest Rate
prompt: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the effective annual rate of interest i and the effective annual rate of discount d over one period?
solution: If $i$ is the effective annual interest rate, then the present value of 1 due in one year is $v = 1/(1+i)$. The effective discount rate is $d = 1 - v = 1 - \frac{1}{1+i} = \frac{i}{1+i}$.

subject: cm1
title: Equivalent Effective Discount Rate
prompt: An investment earns interest at an annual effective rate of 6%. Calculate the equivalent annual effective discount rate (to 4 decimal places).

subject: cm1
title: Force of Interest and Effective Rate
prompt: Which of the following correctly expresses the relationship between the force of interest $\delta$ and the effective annual interest rate $i$?
solution: The force of interest satisfies $1+i = e^{\delta}$, so $\delta = \ln(1+i)$.

subject: cm1
title: Effective Rate from Force of Interest

subject: cm1
title: Compound Interest Definition

options: Interest is earned on both the original principal and previously earned interest
Interest is earned only on the original principal
Interest is deducted from the principal each period
The accumulated value increases linearly over time
solution: Under compound interest, interest is earned on accumulated balances, causing exponential growth.

subject: cm1
title: Accumulating a Single Sum
prompt: An amount of 1 is invested for 5 years at an annual effective interest rate of 4%. Calculate the accumulated value (to 4 decimal places).
solution: Accumulated value: $(1.04)^5 = 1.2166529 \approx 1.2167$.

subject: cm1
title: Time Value of Money
prompt: Which of the following best describes the time value of money?
options: A unit of money today is worth more than the same unit in the future
Money has the same value regardless of time
Future money is always worth more than present money
Time value only applies under inflation
solution: The time value of money reflects preference for earlier receipt due to earning potential and uncertainty.

subject: cm1

subject: cm1
title: Accumulation Under Constant Force
prompt: Which of the following represents the accumulation function $A(t)$ under a constant force of interest $\delta$?
solution: With constant force of interest, accumulation follows $A(t) = e^{\delta t}$.

subject: cm1
title: Meaning of Discounting
prompt: Which of the following best explains the meaning of discounting?
options: Finding the present value of a future amount
Calculating future value of a present amount
Ignoring the time value of money
solution: Discounting converts future cashflows into their present values.

subject: cm1
title: Constant Force from Growth
prompt: An investment grows from 100 to 160 over 8 years at a constant force of interest. Calculate δ (to 4 decimal places).
solution:
Using $160 = 100e^{8\delta}$:
$e^{8\delta} = 1.6 \Rightarrow \delta = \dfrac{\ln 1.6}{8} = \dfrac{0.470004}{8} = 0.0587505$.
To 4 decimal places, $\delta = 0.0588$.

subject: cm1
title: Simple Interest Definition
prompt: Which of the following statements about simple interest is correct?
options: Interest is calculated only on the original principal
Interest is earned on accumulated interest
Simple interest is the standard assumption in finance
solution: Simple interest accumulates linearly since interest is earned only on the principal.

subject: cm1
title: Checking Redington's Conditions
prompt: An insurer's assets and liabilities have equal present values. The assets have (volatility-based) duration 5 and convexity 40; the liabilities have duration 5 and convexity 30. Which of Redington's duration and convexity conditions are satisfied?
options: Both the duration and convexity conditions
solution:
Redington's conditions (at the current rate) are:
1. $PV_A = PV_L$ (given).
2. Duration of assets = duration of liabilities: $5 = 5$, satisfied.
3. Convexity of assets > convexity of liabilities: $40 > 30$, satisfied.
So both the duration and convexity conditions hold, and the insurer is immunised against small changes in interest rates.

solution: The PV of a perpetuity-immediate paying 1 per period is $a_{\overline{\infty}|} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} v^k = \dfrac{v}{1-v} = \dfrac{1}{i}$.

subject: cm1
title: Redemption Yield of a Discount Bond
prompt: A bond has annual coupons of 60 (paid in arrear), face value 1,000 redeemable at par, and 5 years to maturity. Its price is 980. Calculate the gross redemption yield (annual effective), to 4 decimal places.
solution:
Solve $980 = 60\,a_{\overline{5}|} + 1000v^5$.
Starting guess: $i \approx \dfrac{60 + (1000-980)/5}{(1000+980)/2} = \dfrac{64}{990} = 0.0646$; at 6.46% the price is 980.67, slightly too high, so the yield is a little higher.
Solving numerically: $i = 0.06481 \approx 0.0648$.

prompt: A bond with face value 1,000 pays annual coupons of 60 in arrear for 3 years and is redeemed at par. The market price is 970. Calculate the gross redemption yield (annual effective), to 4 decimal places.
solution:
Solve $970 = 60\,a_{\overline{3}|} + 1000v^{3}$ for $i$.
Starting guess (approximation): $i \approx \dfrac{C + (F-P)/n}{(F+P)/2} = 0.0711$. At this rate the price is 970.93, which is higher than 970, so the yield is slightly higher.

subject: cm1
title: Bounds for an Optional Redemption Date
prompt: A bond redeemable at par has an optional redemption date (the borrower may redeem at any time in a given window). The coupon rate is lower than the investor's required yield. Which of the following correctly gives the upper and lower bounds for its present value?
options: Upper bound = earliest redemption PV, Lower bound = latest redemption PV
Upper bound = sum of coupons only, Lower bound = face value only
Upper and lower bounds are always equal
Upper bound ignores interest, lower bound ignores principal
solution:
When the coupon rate is below the yield, the bond is valued below par and the investor gains on redemption, so the earlier that gain is received, the higher the PV.
Hence the upper bound is the PV assuming the earliest redemption date and the lower bound is the PV assuming the latest redemption date. (If the coupon rate exceeded the yield, the bounds would be reversed.)

options: Determining interest rates, repayments, and PVs of financial instruments
Setting all payments equal to zero
solution: Equation of value allows solving for unknown financial quantities by equating PVs at a reference date.

subject: cm1
title: NPV of a Three-Year Project
prompt: A project requires 50,000 and produces cashflows of 20,000 per year for 3 years. At i=8%, compute NPV (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: IRR as a Break-Even Rate
prompt: Which of the following best describes IRR?
options: Initial investment divided by total inflows
solution: IRR is the rate at which the PV of inflows equals PV of outflows.

subject: cm1
title: Instalments on a 7,500 Loan
prompt: A loan of 7,500 is to be repaid in 3 equal annual instalments at i=5%. Calculate annual repayment (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Running Yield Property
prompt: Which of the following statements about running yield is true?
options: Annual coupon divided by current market price
solution: Running yield = annual coupon / current price.

subject: cm1
title: Perpetual Rental at 6%
prompt: A property yields 15,000 per year indefinitely. Interest rate = 6%. Calculate PV (to 2 decimals).
solution: PV perpetuity = Payment / i = 15,000 / 0.06 = 250,000.

subject: cm1
title: Whole-Life Assurance Definition
prompt: Which of the following best describes a whole-life assurance?
options: Pays a sum on death whenever it occurs
Pays a sum if death occurs within a fixed term
Pays a sum at the end of a fixed term regardless of survival
Pays a sum periodically while the person is alive
solution: Whole-life assurance provides a benefit payable on death whenever it occurs, with no fixed term.

subject: cm1
title: Term Assurance Payment Condition
prompt: A temporary assurance pays 50,000 if death occurs in the next 10 years. Which statement is true?
options: It only pays if death occurs within the 10-year term
It pays regardless of death timing
It accumulates a fund payable at maturity
solution: A temporary assurance is term-limited; benefits only occur if death happens within the specified term.

subject: cm1
title: Pure Endowment Definition
prompt: Define pure endowment.
options: Pays a sum only if the person survives to a fixed future date
Pays a sum on death at any time
Pays a combination of death and survival benefits
solution: A pure endowment is contingent on survival to a specific date; no payment occurs if death occurs earlier.

subject: cm1
title: Whole-Life Annuity Definition
prompt: A whole-life annuity pays 1,000 annually in arrear for life. Which is true?
options: Payments continue as long as the annuitant is alive
Payments stop after a fixed term
Payments are only made in advance
solution: A whole-life annuity pays periodically for the entire remaining lifetime of the annuitant.

subject: cm1
title: Endowment Assurance Definition
prompt: Which of the following describes an endowment assurance?
options: Pays either on death within a term or on survival to the end of the term
Pays only on death regardless of term
Pays a fixed periodic amount while alive
solution: Endowment assurances provide benefits on death within a term or survival to the end of the term.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Deferred Life Annuity
prompt: A life aged $x$ buys a deferred whole-life annuity of 2,000 per year payable annually in arrear, deferred for 5 years (so the first payment is at age $x+6$ if alive). Given $\delta = 0.05$, ${}_5p_x = 0.92$ and $a_{x+5} = 15.0$, calculate the expected present value at issue (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Conventional With-Profits Bonuses
prompt: Which statement is true about conventional with-profits contracts?
options: Benefits are increased by regular reversionary bonuses and terminal bonuses
Benefits are fixed and never change
Benefits are only linked to unit prices
Benefits are paid continuously regardless of bonuses
solution: Conventional with-profits policies increase benefits via bonuses.

subject: cm1
title: Unit-Linked Death Benefit
prompt: A unit-linked policy provides death benefit equal to units times unit price. Which is true?
options: Death benefit depends on fund value at death
Death benefit is guaranteed and fixed
Death benefit is only via cash bonuses
solution: Unit-linked benefits are proportional to the fund value expressed as units times current unit price.

subject: cm1
title: Accumulating With-Profits Mechanics
prompt: Under an accumulating with-profits policy, premiums are credited to a policy fund. Which of the following is correct?
options: Fund increases by guaranteed and bonus interest plus terminal bonus
Fund pays benefits immediately without accumulation
solution: Accumulating with-profits policies grow via guaranteed interest, regular bonuses, and terminal bonus.

subject: cm1
title: Life Table Function l_x
prompt: The life table function $l_x$ represents:
options: The (expected) number of lives alive at exact age $x$
The number of deaths at age $x$
The probability of dying within 1 year
The future lifetime of a life aged $x$
solution: $l_x$ is the expected number of lives alive at exact age $x$, out of a starting cohort of $l_0$ (or $l_\alpha$) lives.

subject: cm1
title: Life Table Function d_x
prompt: In a life table, $d_x$ represents:
options: The number of deaths between ages $x$ and $x+1$
The number of survivors at age $x$
The probability of surviving one year
solution: $d_x = l_x - l_{x+1}$, the number dying between exact ages $x$ and $x+1$.

subject: cm1
title: Notation for Survival Probability
prompt: The probability that a life aged $x$ survives $n$ years is denoted by:
solution: ${}_np_x$ is the probability that a life aged $x$ survives to age $x+n$.

subject: cm1
title: Notation for Death Probability
prompt: The probability that a life aged $x$ dies within $n$ years is denoted by:
solution: ${}_nq_x = 1 - {}_np_x$ is the probability of dying within $n$ years.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of an Immediate-Payment Whole-Life Assurance
prompt: A whole-life assurance pays 100,000 immediately on death. Given $\delta = 0.05$ and $\bar{A}_x = 0.6$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Term Assurance
prompt: A temporary (term) assurance pays 50,000 if death occurs within 10 years. Given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{10}|} = 0.08$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Continuous Annuity-Assurance Identity
prompt: Which relationship between whole-life annuity and assurance functions is correct?
solution: Since $\bar{A}_x = E[v^{T_x}]$ and $\bar{a}_x = E\left[\dfrac{1 - v^{T_x}}{\delta}\right]$, we get $\bar{a}_x = \dfrac{1 - \bar{A}_x}{\delta}$, i.e. $\bar{A}_x = 1 - \delta\,\bar{a}_x$.

subject: cm1
title: Curtate vs Continuous Annuities
prompt: Curtate annuity differs from continuous annuity because:
options: Benefits are paid at death only
solution: Curtate annuities pay at integer time points, unlike continuous annuities.

subject: cm1
title: Select Mortality Concept
prompt: What is the key feature of select mortality?
options: Survival probabilities differ for first year(s) after selection
solution: Select life tables account for improved survival in first r years post-selection.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Joint-Life Assurance
prompt: A joint-life assurance pays 100,000 at the end of the year of the first death of $(x)$ and $(y)$. Given $A_{xy} = 0.45$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Last-Survivor Annuity
prompt: A last-survivor annuity pays 1,000 annually while either $(x)$ or $(y)$ is alive. Given $a_{\overline{xy}} = 18.0$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Multiple-Decrement Tables
prompt: Which statement is correct about multiple-decrement tables?
options: They model several competing risks for decrement
They assume only one decrement type
solution: Multiple-decrement tables allow evaluation of multiple causes of decrement simultaneously.

subject: cm1
title: Force of Decrement Meaning
prompt: The force of decrement $\mu_x$ in a continuous model represents:
options: Instantaneous rate of decrement at age x
Number of deaths between x and x+1
solution: $\mu_x = \lim_{h \to 0^+} \dfrac{{}_hq_x}{h}$: the instantaneous rate of decrement at exact age $x$.

subject: cm1
title: Independent Decrements
prompt: In a multiple-decrement model, independent decrements mean:
options: Occurrence of one decrement does not affect probability of others
solution: Independence implies one type of decrement does not affect the probability of others.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of Benefits Under a Single Decrement
prompt: Expected present value of benefits under single decrement equals:
options: Sum over ages of PV * probability of decrement at that age
solution: $EPV = \sum_t v^t \times \text{Benefit}_t \times \Pr(\text{decrement at time } t)$.

subject: cm1
title: Endowment Annuity-Assurance Identity
prompt: Select the correct formula linking the continuous temporary life annuity to the continuous endowment assurance:
solution: With $T = \min(T_x, n)$, $\bar{a}_{x:\overline{n}|} = E\left[\dfrac{1 - v^{T}}{\delta}\right]$ and $\bar{A}_{x:\overline{n}|} = E[v^{T}]$ (an endowment assurance pays at death or at time $n$). Hence $\bar{a}_{x:\overline{n}|} = \dfrac{1 - \bar{A}_{x:\overline{n}|}}{\delta}$.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Deferred Whole-Life Assurance
prompt: A deferred whole-life assurance pays 100,000 on death, with the cover deferred 5 years. Given ${}_{5|}A_x = 0.55$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Temporary Annuity-Due
prompt: A temporary annuity-due pays 1,000 annually for 10 years to a life aged $x$. Given $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{10}|} = 8.5$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Select Life Tables
prompt: Which statement is correct about select life tables?
options: They account for improved survival in first r years after selection
They are identical to ultimate tables
They are only used for annuities
solution: Select tables consider improved short-term survival after selection compared to ultimate tables.

subject: cm1
title: Last-Survivor Annuity Valuation
prompt: A last-survivor annuity pays 500 per year while at least one of $(x)$ and $(y)$ is alive. Given $a_{\overline{xy}} = 20$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Joint-Life Assurance Factor
prompt: Joint-life assurance pays at first death. Which factor is used for PV?
solution: A joint-life assurance pays on the first death, so its EPV uses $A_{xy}$, the assurance factor on the joint-life status.

subject: cm1
title: Endowment Assurance Benefits
prompt: Which describes a temporary endowment assurance?
options: Pays on death within term or on survival to term end
Pays on death at any time
solution: Temporary endowment combines term assurance (death) and pure endowment (survival) payments.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Whole-Life Annuity-Due
prompt: A whole-life annuity-due pays 1,000 per year to a life aged $x$. Given $\ddot{a}_x = 12.5$, calculate the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Deferred Temporary Annuity
prompt: A deferred temporary annuity pays 1,000 annually for 10 years, deferred 3 years. Given ${}_{3|}a_{x:\overline{10}|} = 7.5$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Dependent Decrements
prompt: In multiple decrement models, dependent decrements mean:
options: Occurrence of one decrement affects probability of others
Occurrence of one decrement independent of others
solution: Dependent decrements mean the probability of one decrement can alter the probability of another.

subject: cm1
title: Unit-Linked Benefit Dependence
prompt: A conventional unit-linked policy provides death benefits as units times unit price. Which is correct?
options: Death benefit depends on fund value at death
Benefit paid regardless of fund value
solution: Unit-linked benefits are proportional to current fund value.

subject: cm1
title: Whole-Life Annuity-Due as a Sum
prompt: Select the correct formula for the curtate whole-life annuity-due $\ddot{a}_x$:
solution: $\ddot{a}_x = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} v^k\,{}_kp_x$: the payment of 1 at time $k$ is made if the life survives to $x+k$.

subject: cm1
title: Force of Mortality and q_x
prompt: Assuming the force of mortality is constant at $\mu_x$ over the year of age $x$ to $x+1$, $q_x$ is related to $\mu_x$ by:
solution: With constant force over the year, $p_x = e^{-\mu_x}$, so $q_x = 1 - e^{-\mu_x}$.

subject: cm1
title: Last-Survivor Annuity EPV II
prompt: A last-survivor annuity pays 1,000 per year while either $(x)$ or $(y)$ is alive. Given $a_{\overline{xy}} = 18.0$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Joint-Life Assurance EPV II
prompt: A joint-life assurance pays 100,000 on the first death of $(x)$ and $(y)$. Given $A_{xy} = 0.45$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Accumulating With-Profits Fund Growth
prompt: Which statement about accumulating with-profits contracts is correct?
options: The fund grows at a guaranteed rate plus bonus interest, with a possible terminal bonus
The fund is fixed and never increases
Benefits are paid immediately without accumulation
solution: Premiums are credited to a fund that grows at a guaranteed interest rate plus discretionary (regular) bonus interest; a terminal bonus may be added when the benefit is paid.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a 5-Year Annuity-Due
prompt: A temporary annuity-due pays 500 annually for 5 years. Given $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{5}|} = 4.6$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Temporary Annuity and Endowment Link
prompt: Select the correct relationship between continuous temporary annuity and endowment assurance factors:
solution: $\bar{A}_{x:\overline{n}|} = 1 - \delta\,\bar{a}_{x:\overline{n}|}$, where $\bar{A}_{x:\overline{n}|}$ is the endowment assurance (paying on death within $n$ years or on survival to $n$). Rearranging gives $\bar{a}_{x:\overline{n}|} = (1 - \bar{A}_{x:\overline{n}|})/\delta$.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Pure Endowment
prompt: A pure endowment pays 50,000 at the end of 10 years if the life aged $x$ survives. Given ${}_{10}E_x = 0.7$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Joint-Life Annuity Payments
prompt: Which statement is true about joint-life annuities?
options: Payments continue while all the lives are alive and cease on the first death
Payments stop after a fixed term
Payments are made only at death
Payments are not affected by survival of the lives
solution: A joint-life annuity is payable only while the joint-life status survives, i.e. while all lives are alive; it ceases on the first death. (A last-survivor annuity continues until the second death.)

subject: cm1
title: Select vs Ultimate Mortality
prompt: A select life table adjusts mortality rates for first r years after selection. Which is correct?
options: Mortality lower than ultimate table for first r years
solution: Select tables account for improved short-term survival post selection.

subject: cm1
title: Single Premium for Whole-Life Cover
prompt: A whole-life assurance has sum assured 100,000 payable at the end of the year of death. Given $A_x = 0.6$, calculate the expected present value of the benefit (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: EPV of an Endowment Assurance
prompt: An endowment assurance pays 50,000 on death within 10 years or on survival to the end of 10 years. Given $A_{x:\overline{10}|} = 0.70$, calculate the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Uses of Multiple-Decrement Tables
prompt: Multiple decrement table can be used to model:
solution: Multiple-decrement tables allow for modeling several competing causes of decrement.

subject: cm1
title: Force of Decrement Interpretation
prompt: In a continuous-time model, the force of decrement $\mu_x$ represents:
options: Instantaneous rate of decrement at age x
solution: $\mu_x$ is the instantaneous rate (hazard) of decrement for a life at exact age $x$.

subject: cm1
title: Valuing a Life Annuity-Due
prompt: A curtate whole-life annuity-due pays 1,000 annually. Given $\ddot{a}_x = 12.0$, calculate the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Level Net Premium for Whole-Life Cover
prompt: A whole-life assurance pays 100,000 at the end of the year of death. Level premiums are payable annually in advance for life. Using the equivalence principle with no expenses, and given $A_x = 0.6$ and $\ddot{a}_x = 12.5$, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Prospective Reserve Definition
prompt: In a prospective reserve calculation, which is correct?
options: Reserve = PV of future benefits - PV of future premiums
Reserve = future benefit only, ignoring premiums
solution: Prospective reserve considers present value of future obligations minus future premiums to be received.

subject: cm1
title: Net Premium for an Endowment Assurance
prompt: An endowment assurance pays 50,000 on death within 10 years or on survival to the end of 10 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for 10 years. Given $A_{x:\overline{10}|} = 0.70$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{10}|} = 7.5$, and ignoring expenses, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Retrospective Reserve Definition
prompt: Which statement is true for retrospective reserve?
options: Reserve = accumulated value of past premiums minus accumulated benefits paid
Reserve = present value of future benefits only
solution: Retrospective reserve sums past premiums with interest minus benefits already paid.

subject: cm1
title: Net Premium for a Term Assurance
prompt: A term assurance pays 100,000 at the end of the year of death within 20 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for 20 years. Given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{20}|} = 0.15$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{20}|} = 14$, compute the annual net premium using the equivalence principle (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Death Strain at Risk Definition
prompt: Which is true about death strain at risk?
options: Death strain at risk = sum assured payable on death minus the end-of-year reserve
Death strain = reserve at start of policy
Death strain = PV of future premiums
solution: For policy year $t+1$, $DSAR = S - {}_{t+1}V$: the extra amount the insurer must find if the life dies, over and above the reserve it would otherwise have had to hold.

subject: cm1
title: Mortality Profit Definition
prompt: Mortality profit is:
options: Difference between expected and actual death strain
solution: Mortality profit arises if fewer deaths occur than expected, producing a positive profit.

subject: cm1
title: Premium for a Deferred Whole-Life Assurance
prompt: A deferred whole-life assurance pays 100,000 on death, with cover deferred 5 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for at most 30 years. Given ${}_{5|}A_x = 0.55$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{30}|} = 12$, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Purpose of a Profit Test
prompt: Which is correct for a profit test life insurance model?
options: It projects expected cashflows of premiums, benefits, expenses, and calculates profit over term
solution: Profit testing evaluates the product by projecting all relevant cashflows and determining the profit vector.

subject: cm1
title: Single Premium for a Term Assurance
prompt: Calculate the single net premium for a term assurance with sum assured 50,000, given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{n}|} = 0.07$ (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Gross Premium Reserve Components
prompt: Which statement is correct regarding gross premium reserve?
options: Gross premium reserve accounts for future expenses and premiums
Gross premium reserve = net premium reserve
Gross premium reserve always zero at inception
solution: Gross premium reserve includes both future benefits and expected premiums, accounting for expenses.

subject: cm1
title: Purpose of Non-Unit Reserves
prompt: Unit-linked policy with benefit = units * unit price. What can insurer do to eliminate future negative cashflows?
options: Pay benefits from external funds only
solution: Non-unit reserve allows insurer to adjust for future negative cashflows while keeping unit fund intact.

subject: cm1
title: Prospective Reserve for an Endowment
prompt: Calculate prospective reserve after 5 years for endowment, PV future benefits=40,000, PV future premiums=15,000 (to 2 decimals).
solution: Prospective reserve = PV future benefits - PV future premiums = 40,000 - 15,000 = 25,000.

subject: cm1
title: Recursive Reserve Relationship
prompt: Recursive relationship between successive gross premium reserves allows:
options: Efficient calculation of reserves at each period
solution: Recursive formulas relate reserves from one year to the next, simplifying calculations.

subject: cm1
title: Reserve of a Single-Premium Annuity
prompt: An annuity of 500 per year for 20 years was bought by a single premium at t = 0, so there are no future premiums, and expenses are ignored. The prospective reserve at t = 0 (just after the single premium is paid) is 7,500. Compute the expected present value of future benefits at t = 0 (to 2 decimals).
solution: With no future premiums or expenses, prospective reserve = EPV of future benefits - 0, so EPV of future benefits = 7,500.

subject: cm1
title: Net Premium Valuation
prompt: Which statement is correct for net premium valuation?
options: Reserves are calculated ignoring expenses and using net premiums
Reserves include gross premiums and expenses
Net premium reserve is always zero
solution: Net premium valuation uses pure premiums, ignoring expenses and profit loadings.

subject: cm1
title: Death Strain at Risk Calculation
prompt: A policy has sum assured 100,000 payable at the end of the year of death, and the reserve at the end of that year is 40,000. Calculate the death strain at risk (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Premium from EPV of Benefits
prompt: The expected present value of the benefits under a policy is 10,000. Level premiums are payable annually in advance for 10 years, and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{10}|} = 8.5$. Ignoring expenses, compute the annual net premium using the equivalence principle (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Computing Mortality Profit
prompt: Mortality profit is computed as:
options: Difference between expected and actual claims
Difference between reserve and PV premiums
solution: Mortality profit = expected death strain - actual death strain, i.e. the difference between expected and actual claims (net of reserves released). It is positive when fewer deaths occur than expected.

subject: cm1
title: Single Premium for Death Cover
prompt: A single premium term assurance pays 50,000 on death within the term. Given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{n}|} = 0.08$, and ignoring expenses, compute the single premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Varying Benefit Contracts
prompt: Which statement is true about increasing/decreasing benefit contracts?
options: EPV accounts for change in benefit over time
Death strain unaffected by benefit changes
solution: For increasing/decreasing benefits, EPV calculation reflects varying amounts over time.

subject: cm1
title: Unit-Linked Profit Test Components
prompt: Profit test for unit-linked contract can include:
options: Future unit fund values, non-unit reserves, expenses, and premiums
solution: Unit-linked profit test includes projected unit fund, reserves, premiums, and expenses.

subject: cm1
title: EPV of a Deferred Temporary Annuity-Due
prompt: A deferred annuity-due pays 1,000 per year for 10 years, starting in 5 years' time. Given ${}_{5|}\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{10}|} = 7.0$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Prospective Reserve for an Annuity
prompt: Calculate prospective reserve for annuity, PV future benefits=20,000, PV future premiums=8,000 (to 2 decimals).
solution: Prospective reserve = PV future benefits - PV future premiums = 20,000 - 8,000 = 12,000.

subject: cm1
title: Gross Reserve for Unit-Linked Business
prompt: Which is correct about gross prospective reserve for unit-linked contract?
options: Includes PV of future benefits and PV of future expenses less PV of future premiums
Includes only PV of unit fund
solution: Gross prospective reserve accounts for expected future benefits, expenses, minus premiums.

subject: cm1
title: Net Premium for a 20-Year Term Assurance
prompt: A term assurance pays 100,000 on death within 20 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for 20 years. Given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{20}|} = 0.12$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{20}|} = 15$, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Valuing Deferred Annuities
prompt: Which statement is true for deferred benefit annuities?
options: PV is same as for whole-life annuity
solution: Deferred benefits require discounting from the start of payments, using the deferred annuity factor.

subject: cm1
title: Net Premium for a 15-Year Term Assurance
prompt: A term assurance pays 50,000 on death within 15 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for 15 years. Given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{15}|} = 0.10$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{15}|} = 12$, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Reserve for a Deferred Annuity
prompt: Which is true about the prospective reserve of a deferred annuity?
options: PV of future benefits minus PV of future premiums, considering deferral
solution: Prospective reserve accounts for the deferral period in calculating PV of future benefits and premiums.

subject: cm1
title: Single Premium for Whole-Life Assurance
prompt: Calculate the single net premium for a whole-life assurance with sum assured 100,000, given $A_x = 0.07$ (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Portfolio Mortality Profit
prompt: Which statement is true regarding mortality profit for a portfolio of term assurances?
options: Sum of expected minus actual death strains over portfolio
Difference between reserves and premiums only
PV of future premiums minus PV benefits
solution: Mortality profit aggregates the difference between expected and actual death claims across all policies.

subject: cm1
title: Annuity-Due EPV at Outset
prompt: A whole-life annuity-due pays 1,000 annually. Given $\ddot{a}_x = 10$, calculate the expected present value of future benefits at $t = 0$ (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Gross Prospective Reserve Formula
prompt: Gross prospective reserve is calculated as:
options: PV future benefits + PV expenses - PV future premiums
solution: Gross prospective reserve accounts for all expected cashflows including expenses, minus future premiums.

subject: cm1
title: Premium for a 10-Year Deferred Assurance
prompt: A deferred whole-life assurance pays 100,000 on death, with cover deferred 10 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for at most 30 years. Given ${}_{10|}A_x = 0.45$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{30}|} = 15$, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Death Strain for Annuities
prompt: Which is true about death strain for annuity contracts?
options: Death strain = Benefit due at death - reserve at death
Death strain = EPV of future premiums
solution: In general, death strain = benefit payable on death $-$ reserve released. For an annuity with no death benefit this is $0 - {}_{t+1}V < 0$, so deaths release reserves and generate mortality profit.

subject: cm1
title: Gross Prospective Reserve Calculation
prompt: For a policy, the EPV of future benefits is 50,000, the EPV of future premiums is 20,000 and the EPV of future expenses is 5,000. Calculate the gross prospective reserve (to 2 decimals).
solution: Gross prospective reserve = EPV benefits + EPV expenses - EPV premiums = 50,000 + 5,000 - 20,000 = 35,000.

subject: cm1
title: Single Premium Term Assurance
prompt: Calculate the single net premium for a term assurance with sum assured 50,000, given $A^{1}_{x:\overline{n}|} = 0.09$ (to 2 decimals).
solution: Single premium $= 50{,}000 \times 0.09 = 4{,}500$.

subject: cm1
title: Net Premium Reserve of an Endowment
prompt: Which is true for net premium reserve of an endowment assurance?
options: Calculated ignoring expenses and profit loadings
solution: Net premium reserve uses pure premiums, without including expenses or profit loads.

subject: cm1
title: Profit Vector Definition
prompt: Profit vector in profit test represents:
options: Profit at each time period of the policy
solution: Profit vector shows the net profit (or loss) in each period of the policy from expected cashflows.

subject: cm1
title: Deferred Annuity-Due Valuation II
prompt: A deferred annuity-due pays 1,000 per year for 10 years, starting in 5 years' time. Given ${}_{5|}\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{10}|} = 6.8$, compute the expected present value (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Recursive Gross Premium Reserves
prompt: Which statement is true about recursive gross premium reserve?
options: It links reserve at t to reserve at t+1 for efficient calculation
It only applies to single premium policies
solution: Recursive relationship allows calculation of reserve at each time point from prior reserve and cashflows.

subject: cm1
title: Mortality Profit Calculation
prompt: Calculate the mortality profit if the expected death strain is 30,000 and the actual death strain is 25,000 (to 2 decimals).
solution: Mortality profit = Expected - Actual = 30,000 - 25,000 = 5,000.

subject: cm1
title: Premiums for Increasing Term Assurance
prompt: Which is true about gross premium for increasing benefit term assurance?
options: Premium calculation accounts for benefit increasing over time
solution: Gross premium reflects the expected present value of benefits, including increases over time.

subject: cm1
title: Single Premium for Whole-Life Assurance II
prompt: A whole-life assurance has sum assured 100,000 and $A_x = 0.11$. Ignoring expenses, calculate the single premium (to 2 decimals).
solution: Single premium $= 100{,}000 \times 0.11 = 11{,}000$.

subject: cm1
title: Non-Unit Reserve Role
prompt: Which is true about unit-linked non-unit reserve?
options: Adjusts for future negative cashflows not covered by unit fund
solution: Non-unit reserve ensures negative cashflows are covered without impacting unit fund.

subject: cm1
title: Premium for a 5-Year Deferred Assurance
prompt: A deferred whole-life assurance pays 100,000 on death, with cover deferred 5 years. Premiums are payable annually in advance for at most 25 years. Given ${}_{5|}A_x = 0.5$ and $\ddot{a}_{x:\overline{25}|} = 15$, compute the annual net premium (to 2 decimals).

subject: cm1
title: Prospective Reserve Calculation
prompt: Calculate the prospective reserve if the EPV of future benefits is 45,000 and the EPV of future premiums is 18,000 (to 2 decimals).
solution: Reserve = PV future benefits - PV future premiums = 45,000 - 18,000 = 27,000.

subject: cm1
title: Gross Premium Reserve at Inception
prompt: A gross premium is calculated using the equivalence principle. What is the gross premium prospective reserve at inception (just before the first premium is paid), calculated on the same basis as the premium?
options: Equal to the EPV of the benefits
Always negative, because of initial expenses
solution: By the equivalence principle, EPV of premiums = EPV of benefits + EPV of expenses on the premium basis. The prospective reserve at inception on the same basis is EPV(benefits + expenses) - EPV(premiums) = 0. (On a different, e.g. more prudent, reserving basis it could be positive or negative.)

subject: cm1
title: Drivers of Mortality Profit
prompt: Mortality profit is affected by:
solution: Mortality profit depends on the difference between expected and actual mortality experience.
